metaDescription: Six Scotsman ice makers compared: nugget under-counter machines, a countertop nugget and water dispenser, and gourmet and clear cube undercounter units.
expertTake: The Scotsman UN0815A-1 is the pick for a small commercial kitchen that wants nugget ice in a 15 inch cabinet with front breathing. The Scotsman CU0920MA-1 is the choice for clear cubes with a 57 lb bin at 20 inches wide. Skip the compact countertop dispenser unless people will actually take ice and water all day, because its bin is only a few pounds.
introParagraphs: A commercial ice machine is bought for its ice, its footprint and its service record, in roughly that order. The ice can be soft nugget pellets or clear, full-size cubes, the footprint is set by the width of the cabinet and the way air moves in and out, and the service record shows up years after the sale.

This range spans all three concerns, from narrow under-counter machines that breathe through the front to a countertop dispenser that hands out ice and water without a touch. We compare the models on ice type, output, bin size and the details that cut service calls, then rank who each machine suits.

products.name: Scotsman UN0815A-1 15 in air-cooled nugget undercounter ice maker, 36 lb bin
products.description:
Only 15 inches wide with front breathing and no need for side clearance, the UN0815A-1 is built for the tightest undercounter slots. Output reaches 79 pounds of nugget ice a day, and the cabinet stores 36 pounds in an air-cooled cabinet, a combination that fits a cafe, a break room or a small bar.

The maker adds sealed, maintenance-free bearings that reduce the preventive work on the auger, which is the hardest-working part of a nugget machine. A unit-specific QR code gives quick access to service manuals, cleaning guides and warranty history, a modern touch that saves a phone call to a technician.

Compared with the larger UN324A-1 it makes less and stores less in a much smaller cabinet. Sanitize the bin on a schedule, clean the air filter and descale the water system.
products.bestFor: Small commercial kitchens that want nugget ice in a narrow slot.
pros: 79 lb per day of chewable nugget ice
QR code for manuals and warranty history
cons: 36 lb bin is small for heavy service
Needs a water line and a drain

products.name: Scotsman UN324A-1 undercounter nugget ice maker, 340 lb daily, 80 lb bin
products.description:
At up to 340 pounds a day with an 80 pound bin, the UN324A-1 is the heavy hitter for nugget ice, built for restaurants, hospitals and bars that serve a lot of it. The bin has a slide-back lid that lets staff scoop without lifting a heavy door, and the stainless steel body is designed for a working kitchen.

That scale changes the plumbing and the cooling. It needs a proper water line and drain, and it needs air to carry away a lot of heat. The nugget ice itself is the chewable type that care settings and sports bars favor.

Compared with the 15 inch UN0815A-1 it makes more than four times as much and stores more than twice the ice in a bigger cabinet. Clean the condenser, sanitize the bin and descale the water system.
products.bestFor: Restaurants, hospitals and bars with heavy nugget demand.
pros: 80 lb built-in bin with slide-back lid
cons: Large cabinet and heavy plumbing needs

products.name: Scotsman HID207AX-1 Meridian touch-free countertop nugget ice and water dispenser
products.description:
A touch-free infrared dispenser means a cup under the spout is all it takes, which is why the Meridian suits self-serve counters, care homes and clinics where hands and scoops are a hygiene issue. A countertop body turns out up to 196 pounds of nugget ice a day and adds chilled water.

A UV-LED internal module and sealed maintenance-free bearings cut the frequency and cost of service, two details that matter in a machine that runs all day. Storage is modest because the unit is built to dispense, so the ice is made as it is needed.

Compared with the under-counter nugget models it trades storage for touch-free service and sits on a counter. Keep the dispensing area clean, replace the filter on schedule and descale the water system.
products.bestFor: Self-serve counters and care settings that want hygienic dispensing.
pros: Up to 196 lb per day of nugget ice plus water
cons: Small storage compared with under-counter models
Needs plumbing like any commercial unit

products.name: Scotsman CU0920MA-1 20 in air-cooled cube undercounter ice maker, 57 lb bin
products.description:
A horizontal evaporator is the reason the CU0920MA-1 makes crystal clear cubes: water flows across a flat plate and freezes in layers, pushing out air and minerals. It makes up to 100 pounds a day and holds 57 pounds in a bin, in a cabinet 20 inches wide with front breathing.

The maker emphasizes a rust-free front panel and corrosion-resistant aluminum side panels for a long life, and a unit-specific QR code for manuals and cleaning guides. The 57 pound bin is large for a 20 inch machine and covers the shifts of a busy bar.

Compared with the 15 inch gourmet unit it makes more and stores much more in a slightly wider cabinet. Keep the condenser clean, sanitize the bin and descale the water system on a schedule.
products.bestFor: Bars and restaurants that want clear cubes and a big bin.
pros: Crystal clear cubes from a horizontal evaporator
57 lb bin in a 20 inch cabinet
Rust-free front panel and corrosion-resistant sides
cons: Cube ice only, no chewable option
Needs a water line and a drain

products.name: Scotsman CU50GA-1 15 in undercounter gourmet cube ice maker with bin
products.description:
The CU50GA-1 packs 64 pounds a day of gourmet cubes and a 26 pound bin into a cabinet only 15 inches wide, in a stainless steel body. Gourmet cubes are larger and slower melting than a standard cube, which suits cocktails, spirits and premium service.

The small footprint fits a bar back, a coffee shop or a break room, and the bin is large enough for a modest rush. The output is quoted at optimal conditions of 70 degree air and 50 degree water, so the real figure in a warm kitchen is lower.

Compared with the 20 inch CU0920MA-1 it makes less and stores less in a narrower cabinet. Keep air filters clean, sanitize the bin and descale on a schedule.
products.bestFor: Small bars and cafes that want gourmet cubes in a 15 inch slot.
cons: 26 lb bin is modest for a busy shift

products.name: Scotsman DRCG033A-1SS Legacy 15 in undercounter ice machine, 30 lb per day, 26 lb bin

specList.label: Output
specList.value: 30 lb of extra-large cubes per day

products.description:
The Legacy is the home-kitchen member of the family: 30 pounds a day of extra-large cubes, a 26 pound bin and a stainless steel 15 inch cabinet, sized for a household or a small office rather than a restaurant. The air-cooled condenser uses R290 refrigerant, a hydrocarbon that is efficient and has a low global warming potential.

Extra-large cubes melt slowly and suit spirits and tall drinks. The modest output is a deliberate fit for a home bar, where a lot of storage and a little production beat the opposite. It is the quietest, least demanding machine in this guide.

Compared with the commercial CU50GA-1 it makes about half as much and is aimed at residential use. Maintenance means a clean condenser, a sanitized bin and scheduled descaling.
products.bestFor: Home bars and small offices that want a built-in with a brand name.
pros: 26 lb bin for a home bar
cons: 30 lb per day is low for entertaining on a big scale
Needs a water line and a drain

buyingCriteria.criterion: Nugget, gourmet cube or clear cube
buyingCriteria.explanation: Nugget machines like the UN0815A-1 and UN324A-1 make soft chewable pellets, gourmet cubes from the CU50GA-1 are large and slow melting, and the CU0920MA-1's horizontal evaporator makes crystal clear cubes. Pick the ice that suits your drinks and your customers, because the machines cannot switch.

The UN0815A-1, CU50GA-1 and Legacy are 15 inches wide, the CU0920MA-1 is 20 inches. Several list front breathing with no side clearance, which lets them sit between cabinets. An air-cooled machine in a closed cabinet without airflow overheats, so check the airflow path as well as the width. Leave the maker's stated clearance in front of the unit, keep the air filter clean and avoid placing the machine next to a fryer or an oven that feeds it hot air.

Output runs from 30 pounds on the Legacy to 340 on the UN324A-1, and bins from 26 to 80 pounds. A machine with a big output and a small bin is a dispenser, while one with a big bin and modest output is a reserve. Match both to your peak hour. Count the ice in a typical drink, multiply by drinks per busy hour and make sure the bin can cover that hour with a margin, because the daily output matters little if the bin runs dry at the rush.

Sealed maintenance-free auger bearings on the nugget models cut preventive work, a unit-specific QR code gives access to manuals and warranty history and a UV-LED module on the Meridian reduces sanitation work. These are the details that cut service calls over years.

The Meridian dispenses touch-free with infrared sensing and adds water, which suits self-serve and care settings. Under-counter models have bins you scoop from. A dispenser reduces contact but stores little ice. In a clinic or care home that trade is worth it, because hands and scoops are the main route for contamination, while a bar prefers a big bin it can scoop from quickly.

Every Scotsman here needs a water line and a drain, and one pump-drain model is listed among the family. Check the water pressure, the filter and where the drain sits relative to the machine before you buy, because the plumbing is often the largest installation cost. A floor drain or a standpipe near the machine saves money, while a drain run across a kitchen can double the labor and may need an inspection.

specDecoder.meaning: A design that draws and exhausts air through the front, so side and rear clearance are not needed.
specDecoder.watchFor: The UN0815A-1 and CU0920MA-1 list it; confirm for the others.

specDecoder.meaning: A flat plate that freezes water in layers, pushing out air and minerals to make clear cubes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The CU0920MA-1 uses it; clear cubes melt more slowly.

specDecoder.meaning: Bearings that need no greasing, reducing preventive work on the auger.
specDecoder.watchFor: Listed on the nugget models and the Meridian.

specDecoder.meaning: Output measured at warm 90 degree air and 70 degree water, lower than the cool nominal figure. The gap is often a quarter or more, so size for the lower number.
specDecoder.watchFor: The modular nugget head lists 456 nominal and 333 AHRI; check for each model.

specDecoder.meaning: A hydrocarbon refrigerant with a low global warming potential, used in newer machines.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Legacy lists it; servicing needs a trained technician.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated nugget, gourmet cube and clear cube machines and judged each against its purpose. The UN0815A-1 led nugget, the CU0920MA-1 clear cube. We did not rank across ice types.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and airflow
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 15 and 20 inch widths and front breathing claims. Narrow machines with front airflow scored higher. Large machines were flagged for space.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and bin
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at output from 30 to 340 pounds and bins from 26 to 80 pounds. Balanced pairs scored best. Dispenser designs were judged on dispensing, not storage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Service design
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited sealed bearings, QR service codes and the UV-LED module. These cut service calls. We noted that no design removes the need for cleaning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for use
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched the Legacy to home kitchens and the others to commercial use. Residential suitability and noise counted. We noted where listings give limited detail.

cards.label: Nugget
cards.text: The UN0815A-1, UN324A-1 and Meridian make soft chewable pellets. They suit care homes, bars and coffee shops.

cards.label: Cube
cards.text: The CU0920MA-1, CU50GA-1 and Legacy make clear or gourmet cubes that melt slowly. They suit cocktails and premium service.

howToChoose.note: Nugget for chewing and flavor; cube for slow-melting premium drinks. Many venues keep one of each, with nugget for soft drinks and cubes for the bar.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 15 inch cabinet with front breathing so the machine fits between cabinets with no side clearance.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The UN0815A-1, CU50GA-1 and Legacy are 15 inches wide. The CU0920MA-1 is 20 inches but offers front breathing.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Ice is central to your service. The UN324A-1 and CU0920MA-1 repay in output and bin.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need modest ice at home. The Legacy does the job.

maintenance.task: Clean the air filter and condenser
maintenance.why: Dust and grease block airflow and cut output. A brush or vacuum keeps the machine near spec, and a kitchen with fryers nearby may need the filter cleaned every couple of weeks with the power switched off.
A warm, wet bin grows slime. Use an approved sanitizer and rinse well, empty the bin first and run the machine through a clean cycle before putting it back into service after sanitizing.

Scale coats the evaporator and the auger. Use a maker-approved descaler and rinse thoroughly, then discard the first batch of ice so no cleaning residue reaches a customer, and log the date so the next service is not forgotten.
A clogged filter cuts flow and lets minerals through. Keep a spare on hand, and note the pressure in the line, since low water pressure also cuts ice production and strains the pump.
If the drain backs up, water ends up in the bin or on the floor. A pump drain needs its filter checked.

faq.q: What is the difference between Scotsman nugget and cube machines?
faq.a: Nugget machines scrape a frozen cylinder with an auger to make soft chewable pellets. Cube machines freeze water on a plate to make clear or gourmet cubes.

faq.q: Which Scotsman fits a 15 inch space?
faq.a: The UN0815A-1, CU50GA-1 and Legacy are 15 inches wide, and the UN0815A-1 lists front breathing with no side clearance. That feature matters because many undercounter slots are bounded by cabinets on both sides, and a machine that needs side airflow will overheat in them no matter how well it is plumbed.

faq.q: Do these machines need a drain?
faq.a: Yes. Commercial ice machines need a water line and a drain, and a pump drain is available on some models when the drain sits higher.

faq.q: What does the QR code do?
faq.a: It gives unit-specific access to service manuals, cleaning guides and warranty history, which saves time when something needs attention. In practice it means a technician or a manager can scan the code, see the cleaning steps and check the warranty status without hunting for a paper manual that disappeared years ago.

faq.q: Is the Legacy suitable for a home?
faq.a: Yes. It makes 30 pounds a day of extra-large cubes with a 26 pound bin and is sized for residential use. It is quieter and less demanding than the commercial models, and its low output suits a home bar, though a household that hosts large parties will want to bag ice ahead of time.

faq.q: How long do commercial ice machines last?
faq.a: Many serve for years with regular cleaning, filters and descaling. Neglect shortens that more than heavy use. Most failures start on the water side, with scale on the evaporator or slime in the bin, so a filter, a cleaning calendar and a service contact are worth more than any feature on the spec sheet.
